column8: At 38 weeks, after being told all pregnancy she would deliver by 39 weeks.
column9: Everyone keeps telling me I’ll go late, and I’m annoyed because ever since I started this journey everyone said I would not go that late which was a relief because then I can at least see an end in sight.

column8: Wants a planned date so she can stop work and file leave paperwork.
column9: I said can we please schedule an induction just because I want it on the calendar so I can at least make sure my paperwork is filed correctly with my hr department, and have my away message away and just be in a mental headspace .

column8: Her husband's response to her disappointment at 38 weeks.
column9: My husband has been an absolute saint during my pregnancy, and he’s been absolutely wonderful.

column8: Planning a long drive alone at 12 weeks; asks what is normal.
column9: Yeah just worried about being too sick to drive? I have never been pregnant before so I don’t know what’s normal.

column8: Replying to a curt answer to her question.
column9: I am newly pregnant so I don’t know? Would I be too tired? Too sick? Do people get too sick to drive? I understand driving is fine, this was a question about driving for 4 days straight. God every time I have ever asked to advice here it’s been so snarky!!

column8: Third trimester; her mother-in-law's overstepping, piggybacking on a "vessel" post.
column9: First it was a video of an Ai baby my MIL sent me where the baby states ‘Grandma is my favourite person’ amongst other things. Then booking my C-section date off work without asking me first.

column8: How her partner answers when she is upset with his mother.
column9: My partners response whenever I get upset about his mum is to bring up something my own mum has said.

column8: Her partner's plan for visits to his mother after the birth.
column9: my partner said he will take the baby to see his mum a couple of times a week, which I felt really threatened by and I said I don’t like the thought of him leaving me while he’s literally still in my womb. I just don’t think non-pregnant people understand

column8: First pregnancy in rural Texas; her first midwife appointment at 10 weeks felt like a script.
column9: this is my first baby. I dont know what I dont know. I just wish she had been friendlier, or perhaps offered more information outside of her "spiel".

column8: What the first appointment consisted of.
column9: she rattles off a quick list of things I can't eat or drink

column8: The clinic portal only lets her reply to messages the midwife starts.
column9: I am not able to start a message chain with her through the portal. I can only respond to a chain she starts, and after a few days of inactivity, it cannot be responded to at all.

column8: At 18 weeks, the midwife struggling with the scan machine.
column9: She takes me into a separate room to do an ultrasound and stares at the machine for several seconds before telling me, "I don't know how to work this thing."

column8: One OB and one midwife in town; switching means waiting weeks.
column9: I have looked at other doctors in other towns, but the earliest available one isn't until the end of July, and I'm supposed to have my anatomy scan in two weeks.

column8: What she wants from care and fears missing.
column9: I just want good, consistent care for my baby and I dont know what to do. […] I'm sad that I'm so lost with my first baby. What if she misses something important I need to know?

column8: The answer she kept getting from the midwife to her questions.
column9: All I got was, "it's normal."

column8: A coworker in a two-person office keeps commenting on her size in her second pregnancy.
column9: She went so far as to pull up pictures on her computer of different stages of pregnancy saying “look here, see how small this. You’re at least 35 weeks or your having twins. I’ve seen twins before so I know”.

column8: The coworker complained to their boss about cover around her due date.
column9: She has repeatedly made comments about my size but also how my pregnancy is an inconvenience for her since she was planning on maybe taking vacation the same month as my due date.

column8: At 38+6 with her second, desperate for the end.
column9: And yes before anyone says it, I know baby comes when baby comes. I just need survival tips from women who have BEEN THERE because I am mentally and physically DONE 😭

column8: Waiting days for a scheduled induction.
column9: I’m approved for an elective induction at 39 weeks but they didn’t schedule me until Sunday night and mentally I cannot do 3 more days of this.

column8: Nearly 37 weeks, in pain and wanting other pregnant women to talk to.
column9: I guess I just am looking for some like community. I feel so alone and isolated and just like how tf am I going to do this

column8: After a painful check at 37 weeks.
column9: I’m now so scared of labor and delivery. I’m so scared I’ll be pregnant for three more weeks.

column8: At 14 weeks, tall, struggling with underwear already.
column9: Are the high waisted maternity underwear worth it?

column8: At 36 weeks, her boyfriend's mother started an argument over the baby's name.
column9: His mom caused an argument between us over the name. She claimed I picked the name out with my sisters and that’s why I was set on it, which upset him bc that made it seem like he wasn’t involved in naming our baby.

column8: At 12 weeks in Ontario, after a doctor's visit.
column9: I’ve already seen my doctor and she’s not worried about it but healthcare in Ontario is awful.

column8: First-time mother at 23 weeks, exhausted after feeling better around 14 weeks.
column9: I expected to be tired during pregnancy, but I wasn’t expecting this level of exhaustion in the second trimester.

column8: Why she can't judge her own tiredness.
column9: I don’t have any previous pregnancies to compare it to, so I’m not sure what’s normal.
